answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require every participant to lock a refundable bond in a shared on-chain vault before transacting. Honest agents accrue non-transferable reputation with each successful trade, like sediment slowly hardening into an opal over years - costly to forge, trivial to verify. Attackers can wander freely between cheap throwaway identities, but none of them ever accumulates enough locked stake or history to matter. When fraud is detected, the bond is slashed, so mass-producing fake identities burns real money while buying nothing.
